title: Daayra’s Tepid Weekend: ₹4 Crore Haul Marks Kareena Kapoor’s Lowest in 15 Years
excerpt: Meghna Gulzar's investigative thriller, starring Kareena Kapoor Khan and Prithviraj Sukumaran, collected an estimated ₹4.10–4.50 crore net in its first three days — with a flat Sunday showing no growth.
body:
• Daayra collected an estimated ₹1.75 crore net in India on its third day (Sunday), unchanged from Day 2, taking its three-day domestic total to approximately ₹4.50 crore net, according to box-office tracker Sacnilk.
  • Tracker estimates vary — Pinkvilla puts the weekend slightly lower at ₹4.10 crore, Koimoi higher at ₹5.63 crore — but all agree the film underperformed, with a flat Sunday showing no growth.
  • The total ranks as the lowest opening weekend of Kareena Kapoor Khan’s career in the past 15 years, below The Buckingham Murders’ ₹6.75 crore.
  • The Meghna Gulzar-directed investigative thriller, starring Kapoor and Prithviraj Sukumaran, released on September 18 alongside Kunal Khemu’s Vibe; its modest numbers sit against an unconfirmed reported budget of ₹55 crore.

Meghna Gulzar’s investigative thriller Daayra has finished its first weekend in theatres with a whimper rather than a bang. The film, headlined by Kareena Kapoor Khan and Prithviraj Sukumaran, collected an estimated ₹1.75 crore net in India on its third day — a Sunday — identical to its Day 2 figure, taking its three-day domestic total to approximately ₹4.50 crore net, according to data from box-office tracker Sacnilk.

Tracker estimates vary, but the verdict is consistent. Pinkvilla’s day-wise tally puts the weekend at ₹4.10 crore (₹1.00 crore on Friday, ₹1.50 crore on Saturday, ₹1.60 crore on Sunday), while Koimoi reports a revised total of ₹5.63 crore after a stronger Sunday. The Hindustan Times reported that the film crossed the ₹4 crore mark by Sunday night. The film’s India gross collection stands at roughly ₹5.40 crore.

A flat Sunday ends a subdued weekend

Daayra arrived in cinemas on September 18, opening to a modest ₹1.00–1.15 crore. The Indian Express reported a sharp 89.57 percent jump on Day 2, raising hopes of a turnaround — but the first Sunday brought no growth at all. Sacnilk’s live data placed Sunday occupancy at around 21 percent across 1,839 shows, and the day closed at the same ₹1.75 crore net as Saturday.

The lack of a Sunday bump is the figure that stings most. In the Indian theatrical trade, the first Sunday is typically the peak day of an opening weekend; a flat line there signals weak audience momentum heading into the crucial weekday test. The film also faced direct competition from Kunal Khemu’s Vibe, which released on the same Friday.

The film at the centre of it

Daayra is a crime thriller from Gulzar, produced by Junglee Pictures, built around a confrontation between two senior police officers on opposite sides of a controversial encounter investigation. Kapoor plays DCP Ajooni Kohli, an officer tasked with examining the circumstances surrounding the deaths of four men accused in a brutal crime. Sukumaran plays DCP Raman Kumar, the officer involved in the encounter, who maintains that the accused attempted to escape custody.

The investigation forces Kapoor’s character — and the audience — to weigh whether the encounter was an act of justice or the system taking the law into its own hands. The story draws on the broader public debate surrounding the 2019 Hyderabad rape and murder case and the subsequent police encounter, while presenting its own fictionalised narrative.

“I’ve become a better actor since becoming a mother.”

— Kareena Kapoor Khan

Kapoor, who shares top billing with Sukumaran, has said the role marks a shift in her craft, telling The Shillong Times, “I’ve become a better actor since becoming a mother.” The film is among the year’s most serious-minded Hindi releases — a prestige crime drama rather than a commercial star vehicle.

Where the numbers sit

The weekend total lands Daayra at the very bottom of the opening-weekend rankings for Kapoor’s films over the past 15 years, according to Koimoi’s analysis — below her previous 15-year low, The Buckingham Murders, which managed ₹6.75 crore. For scale, her biggest openers in that period include Singham Again (₹125 crore) and Bajrangi Bhaijaan (₹102.6 crore).

The numbers look particularly modest against reports that Daayra was made on a budget of around ₹55 crore. The makers have not officially confirmed that figure, so it should be treated as an estimate rather than established fact — but even at a fraction of that cost, a sub-₹5 crore opening weekend leaves a long road to recovery.

Trade analysts quoted by Pinkvilla attribute the result to a limited-scope genre and a promotional campaign that failed to cut through, calling the trend one with “nothing to go for.” That said, the film does carry critical backing, and prestige dramas have occasionally outrun weak openings on word of mouth — a thin but real hope.

The diaspora lens

For NRI audiences, the open question is whether overseas markets can cushion the domestic shortfall. Serious-minded Hindi dramas frequently find steadier legs in the United States, the United Kingdom and the Gulf, where Kapoor and Sukumaran both command loyal followings. Overseas figures, typically reported in the first full week, will show whether the diaspora audience is engaging with the film even as domestic footfalls stall.

What to watch next

The Monday hold is the immediate test: whether Daayra can stay above ₹1 crore on its first weekday, or slide the way flat-weekend openers often do. Longer term, the question is whether critical support and conversation around the film’s encounter-justice theme can generate the word of mouth its opening lacked. With Vibe splitting audience attention and no major releases arriving this Friday, the screen count is unlikely to collapse — but the film needs audiences to start showing up.
